patch_description:
The current program has degraded to 0.54 score (from 0.60 in the prior seed) despite adding complexity. The mid-rotation layer (_build_mid_rotation_layer) added 4 new distinct parameters (ry_mid_even, ry_mid_odd, rz_mid_even, rz_mid_odd) and increased gate count from 72 to 120, yet validation accuracy dropped from 0.97 to 0.91 and worst_group_margin stayed flat at 0.30.

This is a classic case of over-parameterization hurting generalization in few-shot learning. The scoring rubric heavily penalizes parameter count: "fewer distinct trainable parameter names ALWAYS scores higher, with no point of diminishing returns."

Strategy: Revert to the simpler, proven structure from the prior seed program (7 distinct parameters), but keep the improved layer organization. This restores:
- Parameter economy (7 vs 11 distinct params)
- Empirically validated architecture
- Better generalization on hard groups

The reversion removes the mid-rotation block entirely and uses the minimal, parity-shared rotation and entanglement pattern that achieved 0.60.
